text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card (17.6%, 272, 4.3%, 4.03, 2.30, 15% ~ 14.6%, 0 documented). The summary is cautious and honestly says records are missing, which is the right framing. But it is thin: the headline is generic and the summary says nothing about the high-complexity 99215 pattern. The by-complexity gradient (55.6% at 5+ conditions vs 7-8% at 0-1) is not used. It gives the excess count (36.4) only implicitly (not at all), and the two cited claims are low-complexity ones with no contrast against high-complexity claims. Next steps are vague (no specific claim IDs for documentation request, 'larger sample' without a size). The investigator would still need to redo some analysis.","problems":["Headline 'too few returned records to judge' is not informative about the billing pattern; the strong statistical signal (4.13x expected, z 2.30) is buried.","Does not use the complexity breakdown: 99215 share rises to 55.6% for 5+ conditions, which suggests part of the pattern is plausibly supported by complexity; this nuance is missing.","Excess 99215 claims (36.4) and ratio 4.13 are omitted.","Only two example claims, both low complexity; no high-complexity counterexample and no mention of 99214 claims with similarly low complexity.","Next steps are generic: no specific claim IDs for the documentation request and no sample size; 'Re-screen once records arrive' is vague.","Says '15%' of 99215 claims were on 0-1 condition patients without noting it is 14.6% (7 of 48) or the count, and does not mention that the packet lists 7 such claims.","Redundant statements about records ('Records came back for 0 claims' and 'No documented 99215 claims came back')."]}
